title: Reverse-engineering workshop
description: Study how a product you like is built, and turn the study into the first stages of your own product.
keywords: reverse engineering, product study, product planning

blocks.title: Study a product you admire. Build your own on its ideas.
blocks.description: Send the address of a site or app you like. We study how it is built: its pages, its flows and the SDK it ships. Then we write one report that becomes the first stages of your own product.

blocks.title: From an address to your first stages
blocks.note: Each step needs the one before it.

steps.title: Send an address
steps.text: Send the address of a site or app, or screenshots if its rules forbid study.

steps.title: We study it
steps.text: We look at its pages, its flows and the SDK it ships, the way a user and a developer would see them.

steps.title: You get a report
steps.text: The report describes how the product works, in our own words. The product quiz turns it into stages 0 to N of your product.

blocks.title: What we study, and what we never copy

blocks.text: A report describes how a product is built and how its parts work together. It is written in our own words.

items: Studied: pages, flows from start to finish, and the SDK in the form it ships to developers.
Never copied: the code, texts, images, design and data of the product.
Never done: signing in to someone else's account, or getting past a protection.
When a site forbids study, the source becomes screenshots that you take yourself.

blocks.text: The report goes to the product quiz, where you decide what your own product will be. The study gives you a starting point, not a copy.

items.q: Do I need an account on the site I study?
items.a: Only for pages behind a sign-in, and only in a test account that belongs to you. We never see a password.

items.q: Will my product look like theirs?
items.a: No. Their design is not copied. The report describes the ideas behind the product, and your product gets its own design.

items.q: What do I get at the end?
items.a: One report in plain words, which the product quiz turns into the first stages of your product.
Not every site allows it. If its rules forbid study, send screenshots instead.
